feature: API-key classic device accepts Python or API field names in mappings
description: networks.create_classic_device_with_api_key accepts credential and device mappings keyed by either the model's Python field names or Forward's API names. It always sends API names, refuses a field spelled both ways, keeps its existing checks whatever the spelling, passes unknown keys through unchanged, and leaves model arguments unchanged.

specs.description: Python-named credential and device fields are sent under their API names
specs.given: A credential mapping {"name": "k", "type": "API_KEY", "password": "secret", "login_type": "API_KEY", "auto_associate": false} and a device mapping {"name": "edge-1", "host": "10.0.0.1", "cli_credential_id": "C-1"}, with a transport that records every request
specs.then: The recorded credential request body names the fields loginType and autoAssociate, carrying the values API_KEY and false. The recorded device request body names cliCredentialId with the value C-1. name, host, type and password keep the same spelling.

specs.description: A mapping that already uses API names is sent with those names
specs.given: A credential mapping {"name": "k", "type": "API_KEY", "password": "secret", "loginType": "API_KEY"} and a device mapping {"name": "edge-1", "host": "10.0.0.1", "cliCredentialId": "C-1"}
specs.then: The credential request body carries loginType with the value API_KEY. The device request body carries cliCredentialId with the value C-1.

specs.description: No Python field name reaches Forward when it differs from the API name
specs.given: A credential mapping that uses login_type and auto_associate, and a device mapping that uses cli_credential_id
specs.when: create_classic_device_with_api_key is awaited and the request bodies are recorded
specs.then: None of the request bodies contains the key login_type, auto_associate or cli_credential_id.

specs.description: For every field, both spellings produce the same request
specs.given: Any model field F of NewHttpCredential or NewClassicDevice with Python name p and API name a, and any value v the model accepts for F, other than a device's http credential
specs.when: Valid otherwise-identical mappings are sent once with {p: v} and once with {a: v}
specs.then: Both calls produce request bodies that carry a: v. Neither body carries p unless p equals a. The two recorded bodies are equal.

specs.description: A device field named both ways with differing values is refused before any request
specs.given: A valid API_KEY credential mapping and a device mapping {"name": "edge-1", "host": "10.0.0.1", "cli_credential_id": "C-1", "cliCredentialId": "C-2"}
specs.then: It raises ValueError and the transport records no request.

specs.description: A field named both ways is refused even when the two values agree
specs.given: A credential mapping {"name": "k", "type": "API_KEY", "password": "secret", "login_type": "API_KEY", "loginType": "API_KEY"} and a valid device mapping
specs.then: It raises ValueError and the transport records no request.

specs.description: A mapping that names each field once is not refused, even if it mixes spellings
specs.given: A credential mapping that uses login_type and autoAssociate, each once, and a valid device mapping
specs.then: No ValueError is raised for duplicate spelling. The credential request is sent with loginType and autoAssociate.

specs.description: Any field present under both spellings causes refusal
specs.given: Either argument given as a mapping, any field F of the target model whose Python name p differs from its API name a, and any values v1 and v2, equal or not
specs.when: The mapping contains both p: v1 and a: v2 and create_classic_device_with_api_key is awaited
specs.then: It raises ValueError and no request is made.

specs.description: A valid API-key credential and named, hosted device without an HTTP credential is accepted
specs.given: A credential mapping {"name": "k", "type": "API_KEY", "password": "secret"} and a device mapping {"name": "edge-1", "host": "10.0.0.1"}
specs.then: No ValueError is raised and requests are sent to Forward.

specs.description: A device naming an HTTP credential by the Python name is refused
specs.given: A valid API_KEY credential mapping and a device mapping {"name": "edge-1", "host": "10.0.0.1", "http_credential_id": "H-1"}
specs.then: It raises ValueError and the transport records no request. No request carries http_credential_id or httpCredentialId.

specs.description: A device naming an HTTP credential by the API name is refused
specs.given: A valid API_KEY credential mapping and a device mapping {"name": "edge-1", "host": "10.0.0.1", "httpCredentialId": "H-1"}
specs.then: It raises ValueError and the transport records no request.

specs.description: A credential whose type is not API_KEY is refused
specs.given: A credential mapping {"name": "k", "type": "LOCAL", "password": "secret", "login_type": "API_KEY"} and a valid device mapping
specs.then: It raises ValueError and the transport records no request.

specs.description: A device with no name or no host is refused
specs.given: A valid API_KEY credential mapping, and in turn the device mappings {"host": "10.0.0.1", "cli_credential_id": "C-1"} and {"name": "edge-1", "cliCredentialId": "C-1"}
specs.when: create_classic_device_with_api_key is awaited with each device
specs.then: Each call raises ValueError and the transport records no request.

specs.description: The checks give the same verdict whichever spelling is used
specs.given: Any credential and device mappings, and the same mappings with any subset of fields renamed between Python name and API name, with no field named both ways
specs.when: create_classic_device_with_api_key is awaited with each version
specs.then: Either both versions raise ValueError before any request, or neither is refused by the name, host, API_KEY-type or HTTP-credential checks. Any mapping that names an HTTP credential under either spelling is always refused before any request.

specs.description: A key the model does not describe is sent unchanged
specs.given: A valid API_KEY credential mapping and a device mapping {"name": "edge-1", "host": "10.0.0.1", "vendorHint": "x"}, where vendorHint is neither a Python nor an API name on NewClassicDevice
specs.then: The device request body carries vendorHint with the value x.

specs.description: Unknown keys are neither refused nor renamed
specs.given: A valid API_KEY credential mapping and a device mapping {"name": "edge-1", "host": "10.0.0.1", "some_extra_field": 1}, where some_extra_field is not a name on NewClassicDevice
specs.then: No ValueError is raised for the unknown key. The device request body carries some_extra_field with the value 1, and does not carry someExtraField.

specs.description: Every unknown key passes through unchanged
specs.given: Any otherwise valid mapping and any key k that is neither a Python nor an API name of the target model's fields, with any value v
specs.when: The mapping includes k: v and create_classic_device_with_api_key is awaited
specs.then: The corresponding request body carries exactly k: v, and the call is not refused because of k.

specs.description: Model arguments are serialized with to_api()
specs.given: A NewHttpCredential model of type API_KEY and a NewClassicDevice model with name and host set and no HTTP credential
specs.when: create_classic_device_with_api_key is awaited with the models
specs.then: The credential request body equals credential.to_api(), and the device's caller-supplied fields appear as in device.to_api().

specs.description: A model argument is not re-keyed into Python names
specs.given: A NewHttpCredential model with login_type and auto_associate set, and a valid NewClassicDevice model
specs.then: The credential request body does not contain login_type or auto_associate. It contains loginType and autoAssociate, as to_api() gives.

specs.description: For any credential model, the body is exactly to_api()
specs.given: Any valid NewHttpCredential model m of type API_KEY and a valid device
specs.then: The credential request body equals m.to_api().
